rationale: Both parse the board identically and run the same correct DFS with the same hex-neighbour generator. The difference is how each player's edges are specified. A passes explicit start and end coordinate lists into _has_path, so the search function stays generic and the call sites in get_winner show exactly which sides each player connects. B passes magic strings ("left", "right", "top", "bottom") and branches on them inside _connects with conditional expressions and an inner closure. That stringly typed interface is more fragile and harder to read. B's class docstring is a nice addition, and its edge check avoids building an end set, but A's cleaner abstraction makes it the better design.
